scope: Synthetic source app; fixture seeded explicitly, later controls/pointer operations real
checks: existing on-scan pointer mode projects the point onto the mesh without a 3D offset
normal numeric movement persists a signed off-scan node target
numeric movement creates exactly one local Undo
changing the motion axis never reinterprets or moves the point
captured 3D drag blocks Create without disabling live preview
a second pointer cannot change the active gesture
Ctrl+Z cannot interrupt an active 3D gesture; Escape owns cancellation
global and local Undo controls are disabled during the captured gesture
Escape restores the entire pre-drag node state and history
a completed pointer drag contributes one local Undo and releases capture
real pointer drag changes the 3D target
editing a point does not rotate or reset the shared camera
local Undo restores the exact previous 3D targets
local Redo restores the exact completed drag
an internal shared-curve grip can leave the scan too
UI distinguishes scan projection from unimplemented 3D scan/CAD magnet
native save contains all node/grip offsets, not a flattened preview
fresh-page rebuild retains node and grip targets
reopened CAD keeps four sewn faces with measured shared gap below 0.005 mm
independent OCCT validates the exported four-face CAD sheet
derived internal centre has a persistent normal displacement
internal centre preview is lifted without losing any baseline-produced patch
internal centre Undo removes only its explicit offset
internal centre Redo restores the normal displacement
native save retains the derived-centre displacement
synthetic scan input is byte-for-byte unchanged
no application console errors
centreLimit: This planar triangular fixture already produces only two patches before movement; this UI case is not a qualification of all three sectors. The separate curved-cap OCCT test checks three sewn faces.
